scoring_justification: Re-running the full RFA computation in the checker is infeasible (requires orbital databases and heavy integration), so we compare the agent's computed values at the paper's reported q points to the published gold with an absolute tolerance. A lightweight integral recompute provides a T1 consistency boost.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold Compton profile values for Neckel and Lye configurations at Table 1 q points
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Table 1 of the paper (1987 J. Phys. C: Solid State Phys. 20 5415)
hidden_assets.generation_method: Manually transcribed from the paper's published table.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact reported values from the paper; they serve as the authoritative reproduction target.

outputs.description: Compton profile values J(q) for TiC computed with the RFA model, convoluted with the instrumental resolution function (Gaussian, FWHM=0.41 au), for two charge configurations, normalized to 12.10 electrons over [0,5] au. Values for q=0.0,0.1,...,5.0 au.

output_contract.notes: Convolution step added to match the gold values from the paper's Table 1.

steps.description: Ensure CSV exists, has required columns, and sufficient rows.
Compare J_RFA_Neckel and J_RFA_Lye values at Table 1 q points against paper's published values within absolute tolerance 0.01; score as fraction of correct points.
Verify the integrated area under J(q) from 0 to 5 au equals 12.10 (within 0.1 electrons) for both columns.
